meetings.headline: Commission flagged unresolved contamination as a threat to the town's plan to RFP the old Main Ave gas station site

what_happened.line: Commission voted to send a formal letter pressing the responsible party to repair the steeple at the 50 Main Street church.
The letter must go out by January 20 regardless, after town counsel gets seven business days to review the draft.
The chair offered to personally cover a mailing cost if it became an obstacle to sending the letter on time.
The commission welcomed newly appointed commissioner Jennifer Sanderson, who also serves on the Historical Commission.
The next meeting was set for February 12, contingent on the 50 Main Street property's responsible party confirming participation.

why_it_matters: A town preservation body is formally pressing a private property owner to fix a deteriorating landmark, a step that can precede further town involvement if the repair does not happen.
A commissioner personally offering to cover a cost, rather than the town budgeting for it, is not a town expenditure and residents should not read it as one.
The addition of a new commissioner with a seat on two boards touches how preservation and history matters get coordinated going forward.
watch_next: Whether the letter goes out by January 20 and what the responsible party's response is.
The February 12 meeting, contingent on the property owner confirming participation.
